item.title: Estonia's plan to shut Russian border disrupts families on both sides
item.description: As soon as Estonia announced it was shutting its land border with Russia next month, Alla Guseva decided she had to bring her 86-year-old mother home to St Petersburg.
item.content:encoded:
Estonia's plan to shut Russian border disrupts families on both sides As soon as Estonia announced it was shutting its land border with Russia next month, Alla Guseva decided she had to bring her 86-year-old mother home to St Petersburg. Reuters | Updated: 18-11-2026 00:28 IST | Created: 18-11-2026 00:28 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

As soon as Estonia announced it was shutting its land border with Russia next month, Alla Guseva decided she had to bring her 86-year-old mother home to St Petersburg. Her mother had been living on her own in Estonia's capital Tallinn, but with the border shutting it was now too much of a risk to leave her there. "I cannot leave her alone," Guseva told Reuters as she and her mother stood for hours in the queue to exit on the Estonian side, bundled against the cold. Estonia, which along with Baltic neighbours Latvia and Lithuania are the only EU countries that still operate overland border crossings with Russia, announced on Sunday it would close its three crossings from December. It said the measure was necessary after blaming Russia's GRU military intelligence service for ordering an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems. Eight Latvian residents suspected of carrying it out were arrested. "Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences," Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna said on X. The Kremlin said on Monday it "completely rejects" that Russia was behind the attempted arson, and accused Estonia of "building a wall" by closing the border. FAMILIES ON BOTH SIDES Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in Europe to reach St Petersburg a few hours' drive away. Marina Kupchenko, a Russian pensioner living in France, said she regularly travels via Tallinn and Narva to visit her elderly mother in St Petersburg, but the trip, by air over third countries, will now be far more difficult and expensive. "The closure will have a very serious effect on me," she said. "My mother cannot move out, so I must keep visiting her. I am her only daughter." Andrey Kukkonen, 56, from Finland, said he was visiting his wife's mother living in Russia. Since Finland shut down its own Russian border in 2023, the trip now takes him 24 hours. It will take three days if Estonia closes its border, he said. "This is politics and it's leading nowhere. The only outcome is people who have relations across the border will start to cut them. Why?" Of the 760,000 people who crossed the Estonia-Russia border this year, 307,000 were Russian nationals, 175,000 were Estonian citizens and 54,000 held Finnish passports, Estonian police data showed. Katri Riik, a former mayor of Narva, said local businesses will take a hit from the lack of visitors, further depressing the economy in a remote corner of the EU. "People in Narva do not understand why this measure is needed, especially ahead of Christmas and New Year," she said. "We used to pride ourselves on being the gateway to Europe. Now we are becoming its fringe." (Writing by Andrius Sytas Editing by Peter Graff)

item.title: Bangladesh court grants 7-day remand of former Dhaka mayor Saeed Khokon
item.description: A Dhaka court on Tuesday granted a seven-day remand of former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Mayor and Awami League leader Mohammad Saeed Khokon in connection with a case linked to the killing of ...
item.content:encoded:
Bangladesh court grants 7-day remand of former Dhaka mayor Saeed Khokon  A Dhaka court on Tuesday granted a seven-day remand of former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Mayor and Awami League leader Mohammad Saeed Khokon in connection with a case linked to the killing of a man during the July 2024 uprising, amid mounting political tensions over former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh in December. ANI | Updated: 17-11-2026 23:09 IST | Created: 17-11-2026 23:09 IST

Representative Image (File Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

A Dhaka court on Tuesday granted a seven-day remand of former Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Mayor and Awami League leader Mohammad Saeed Khokon in connection with a case linked to the killing of a man during the July 2024 uprising, amid mounting political tensions over former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh in December. Metropolitan Magistrate Mehedi Hasan passed the order after the Detective Branch (DB) of police sought 10 days of remand for questioning Khokon in connection with the killing of Abdul Motaleb during the July Uprising, according to local media reports. Khokon was detained by the Special Response Battalion (SRB) from his residence in Dhaka's Baridhara area at around 7 am on Tuesday and subsequently handed over to the detectives. He was later produced before the court by the DB. According to local media reports, State Prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi supported the police's request for remand, while senior lawyer Abu Sayeed Sagor sought bail for Khokon and cancellation of the remand order. Investigators have alleged that Khokon helped orchestrate the crackdown on protesters during the July 2024 uprising by directing members of the Chhatra League, Jubo League and other Awami League-affiliated organisations to attack demonstrators, while allegedly providing them with money and weapons. The remand petition also accused him of organising surprise party marches after the fall of the Awami League government and maintaining contact with senior party leaders who are currently in hiding. Investigators further alleged that Khokon had planned activities to destabilise the country. The case relates to the killing of Abdul Motaleb, who was shot dead during a procession near the Zigatola bus stand in Dhaka's Dhanmondi area on August 4, 2024. His father, Abdul Matin, filed the case at Dhanmondi Police Station on August 26, 2024, after the fall of the Awami League government. The case names 176 people, including then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former Home Minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal and former Road Transport Minister Obaidul Quader. Khokon's arrest comes amid mounting political tensions following Sheikh Hasina's announcement that she would return to Bangladesh in December. Leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations have reportedly become increasingly active in different parts of the country. Although the activities of the Awami League have been banned in Bangladesh, incidents of violence have continued to be reported in various areas, with the banned party being blamed for several such activities. Gopalganj, Sheikh Hasina's home district, has witnessed some of the significant incidents of violence. Amid the evolving political situation, police and other law enforcement agencies have intensified operations against Awami League leaders and activists. Khokon's arrest is part of these ongoing actions. Khokon, the son of former undivided Dhaka mayor Mohammad Hanif, became the Mayor of Dhaka South City Corporation in 2015. He later won the Dhaka-6 parliamentary constituency as an Awami League candidate in the 2024 parliamentary elections, according to local media reports. (ANI)

item.title: Tiger Woods confirms competitive golf return for December at Bahamas
item.description: This invite-only tournamrnt, hosted by Woods' Foundation has previously served as a comeback event for the golf icon, who has limited his playing time since injuries sustained during a car crash back ...
item.content:encoded:
Tiger Woods confirms competitive golf return for December at Bahamas This invite-only tournamrnt, hosted by Woods' Foundation has previously served as a comeback event for the golf icon, who has limited his playing time since injuries sustained during a car crash back in February 2021. ANI | Updated: 17-11-2026 22:51 IST | Created: 17-11-2026 22:51 IST

Tiger Woods (Photo: Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Golf legend Tiger Woods confirmed his return to competitive action during next month's Hero World Challenge, reported Sky Sports. This invite-only tournamrnt, hosted by Woods' Foundation has previously served as a comeback event for the golf icon, who has limited his playing time since injuries sustained during a car crash back in February 2021. Woods has not appeared on PGA Tour since he missed the cut way back in July 2024. The 15-time major titlist also missed the last season due to Achillies tendon rupture. The golf legend underwent back surgery last October and missed this year's season away, "stepping away" following a car crash in March after which he was charged with reckless driving. The 50-year-old is now scheduled to compete in Bahamas. The event will be held from December 3-6, with 2019 US Open champion Gary Woodland and Rickie Fowler among the other players included in the 20-man field. Woods was absent from the line-up which was initially last month, with Hideki Matsuyama returning as defending champion and Scottie Scheffler gunning for his third title in four years, while Players champion Cameron Young and former US Open winner Matt Fitzpatrick also feature. The multi-time PGA Tour champion currently is the 'unranked' in OWGR standings. The former world number one had made just four 72-hole tournament appearances in last six seasons and has not been in the world's top ten since January 2020. His last appearance at this competition came back in 2023 and had previously won the tournament in 2001, 2004, 2006, 2007 and 2011. (ANI)

item.title: Fresh unrest erupts in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj, Sheikh Hasina’s stronghold
item.description: "Fresh incidents of violence have been reported in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj district, where a police station in Tungipara and several vehicles were set on fire, though details are still awaited", Police ...
item.content:encoded:
Fresh unrest erupts in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj, Sheikh Hasina’s stronghold "Fresh incidents of violence have been reported in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj district, where a police station in Tungipara and several vehicles were set on fire, though details are still awaited", Police spokesperson Kamarun Munira told ANI by phone, without elaboration. ANI | Updated: 17-11-2026 22:23 IST | Created: 17-11-2026 22:23 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Fresh violence has been reported again in Gopalganj, the birthplace and stronghold of Sheikh Hasina, despite heightened security measures. "Fresh incidents of violence have been reported in Bangladesh’s Gopalganj district, where a police station in Tungipara and several vehicles were set on fire, though details are still awaited," police spokesperson Kamarun Munira told ANI by phone, without elaboration. "Leaders and activists of the activity-banned Awami League and the banned Chhatra League have attacked and set fire to the Tungipara Police Station in Gopalganj. On Tuesday evening, they first marched to surround the police station, later attacking the premises and setting fire to multiple vehicles inside the compound", the daily Prothan Alo reported. "To bring the situation under control, police reportedly fired tear gas shells, rubber bullets, and sound grenades. Tension escalated in the area after rumours spread that police had detained several leaders and activists of the banned Awami League. Subsequently, an announcement was made over a mosque's loudspeaker to gather people. At one point, the crowd besieged the Tungipara Police Station and later set it on fire," it added. "Multiple videos of the attack and arson have circulated on the social media platform Facebook. One video shows at least three vehicles burning inside the Tungipara Police Station compound, accompanied by the sounds of vandalism. At the same time, the attackers were seen chanting slogans of "Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu" while carrying sticks and rods. Some were seen recording the attack and arson on their mobile phones," the report said. "In another video, a man named H.M. Rubel Farazi was heard saying during a Facebook Live, "We will burn down the police station shortly." During the broadcast, he also stated that the police had fired tear gas at them, which they were trying to neutralise by lighting fires, adding that they would not back down," Prothom Alo reported. (ANI)
